title: What is known about 1RB0LF_1RC0RB_1LD0RA_0LE0LC_1LB1LF_1LD---
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0LF_1RC0RB_1LD0RA_0LE0LC_1LB1LF_1LD---.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. Its tape is a list of counters, each a run of 01 or 10, which the head sweeps over and updates. This page lists what has been established, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. Lean proves the halting configurations and no halt in the first 107 steps. The counter structure described below is observed in simulations, not proved. No halt in the first 109 steps.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 76,681 cells have been visited and 38,338 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: sqrt/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.554). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.389).

claims.title: Halting needs 1 A>1 or 1 E>1
claims.text: The only halting entry is F reading a 1. F is entered from A>1 (write 0, move left) and from E>1 (write 1, move left), so the machine halts exactly when A or E reads a 1 with a 1 to its left. In the first 108 steps F is entered 27,487 times, always onto a 0; the window around the head is 101[0]101 in 22,690 of them.

claims.title: A list of counters
claims.text: At the left end the tape reads E>0 (01)^a (10)^b (01)^c (10)^d … (the boundaries between runs are single defects, 0 or 1, which change from visit to visit). a grows by one every three left-end visits, b at half that rate; c shrinks while d grows. For example (a, b, c, d) = (284, 167, 242, 19) at step 404,490 and (651, 349, 180, 53) at step 1,315,510.

claims.title: Size of the tape description (family screen)
claims.text: At the 8 records between 2.6·10<sup>8</sup> and 1.7·10<sup>10</sup> steps (first new leftmost or rightmost cell after each threshold 10<sup>6</sup>·4^k) the tape has 39,174 to 337,961 visited cells and compresses to 18 to 27 level-2 tokens (repeats of a word of at most 40 cells, then repeats of groups of such tokens).

claims.title: Proposed family: F06, block-list counters
claims.text: The description grows slowly: 20 to 27 level-2 tokens at every record from 2.6·108 to 1.7·1010 steps, and 11 to 46 runs in the macro simulator (blocks of 4 cells) at the sampled records up to 2·1016 steps. The machine shares its table with 1RB1RF_1LC0LB_1RE0LD_1LB0RF_0RA0RC_1RE--- (states renamed, some of the four mirrored; related.json), started in another state. On the screen the four runs show the same list of blocks at the same moments. For example near step 6.4·107 all four tapes read (mirrored) blocks of 3, 1,546, 39, 1,753, 117, 1,467 and 997 pairs 01 and then a last block, of 4,405 pairs in 1RB1RF_1LC0LB… and of 4,411 pairs here. The four last blocks differ by 2, 4 and 6 pairs and the records come at slightly different steps. This is an observation at the sampled records: it is not a proof that the runs correspond, and nothing about halting is carried over. For 1RB1RF_1LC0LB… the right end is proved in Lean to be a base-3 counter on the separators of such a list (bb6-1RB1RF_1LC0LB/lean/Counter.lean). Those theorems are about that machine's table with its own state names; they apply here only after the renaming is carried through, which has not been done. A list of blocks with a base-3 counter is F06.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. The rates suggest a counter system (the first runs as unary counters that pass amounts down the list), but the defects between the runs and the words at the right end change from visit to visit, and what happens when a shrinking counter reaches 0 (a run disappears and the list is rebuilt) has not been described; both are where a halt could come from.

claims.title: Related holdouts
claims.text: The same table as 1RB0RA_1LC0RE_0LD0LB_1LA1LF_1RA0LF_1LC--- up to renaming, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each. The same table as 1RB1RF_1LC0LB_1RE0LD_1LB0RF_0RA0RC_1RE--- up to renaming and mirroring, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each. The same table as 1RB0LE_0RC0RA_1RD1RF_1LA0LD_1LD0RF_1RB--- up to renaming and mirroring, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. Started on a blank tape, this machine writes a list of numbers, each one a run of 01 or of 10, and sweeps back and forth over the list updating them: the first grows, the second grows at half the speed, the third shrinks. How the list changes when a number runs out is the open part.

facts.text: No halt, checked by Lean's kernel (10<sup>7</sup> by compiled code).
No halt in the C simulator.
Entries into the halting state F in 10<sup>8</sup> steps, all onto a 0.

sections.heading: The two ways to halt
html: The only halting entry is F reading a 1. Two transitions lead to F, both moving left: A reading 1 (writes 0) and E reading 1 (writes 1). So the machine halts exactly when 1 A>1 or 1 E>1 occurs. F is entered rarely, 27,487 times in the first 108 steps, and every time the cell it lands on is a 0, almost always inside the pattern 101[0]101 of a run of 10s.

sections.heading: A list of counters
html: Stop the simulator whenever the head reaches a new cell at the left end and write the tape with runs compressed. Every 50th such moment:

A run of 01s and a run of 10s with a single cell between them are the same counter seen with a different defect: (01)^a (10)^b and (01)^a 0 (01)^b are both a followed by b. Read that way the tape is a list a, b, c, d, … of numbers. a grows by 17 every 50 left-end visits, b by about 8 (half as fast), c shrinks by about 3, d grows by about 4. The last 20 to 100 cells are short irregular words.

Earlier, at step 136,230, the list is (185, 127, 110) and at step 284,618 it is (201, 124, 257): the list is rebuilt when a counter runs out. Those rebuilds are what a proof would have to describe; they are not analysed.

sections.heading: Which family it belongs to
html: The 22 machines of family F09 (“bouncers over lists of counters, not yet classified”) were screened in one way. The machine runs from blank tape for 2·1010 steps; each time the tape reaches a new cell after a threshold, the tape is compressed twice: first repeats of one word, then repeats of groups of words. If the tape is a few growing blocks and a bounded rest, the number of level-2 tokens stays bounded while the tape grows. Everything in this section is observed in one run. None of it is proved.
Proposed family: F06, block-list counters (blocks of pairs with a base-3 counter, as in 1RB1RF_1LC0LB… (same table)).

The description grows slowly: 20 to 27 level-2 tokens at every record from 2.6·108 to 1.7·1010 steps, and 11 to 46 runs in the macro simulator (blocks of 4 cells) at the sampled records up to 2·1016 steps.

The machine shares its table with 1RB1RF_1LC0LB_1RE0LD_1LB0RF_0RA0RC_1RE--- (states renamed, some of the four mirrored; related.json), started in another state. On the screen the four runs show the same list of blocks at the same moments. For example near step 6.4·107 all four tapes read (mirrored) blocks of 3, 1,546, 39, 1,753, 117, 1,467 and 997 pairs 01 and then a last block, of 4,405 pairs in 1RB1RF_1LC0LB… and of 4,411 pairs here. The four last blocks differ by 2, 4 and 6 pairs and the records come at slightly different steps. This is an observation at the sampled records: it is not a proof that the runs correspond, and nothing about halting is carried over.

For 1RB1RF_1LC0LB… the right end is proved in Lean to be a base-3 counter on the separators of such a list (bb6-1RB1RF_1LC0LB/lean/Counter.lean). Those theorems are about that machine's table with its own state names; they apply here only after the renaming is carried through, which has not been done. A list of blocks with a base-3 counter is F06.
Next step. Carry the renaming through, so that the counter theorems of 1RB1RF_1LC0LB… become theorems about this machine, and state exactly how the two tapes differ (the last block and the left end).

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.554). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.389).
After 109 steps the tape spans 76,681 cells (39,631 left of the start, 15,537 right), with a density of 1s of 0.5.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: Related machines
html: Other holdouts of the list of 608 that are tied to this one. The comparison of tables is exact; everything about runs was checked on the first 107 steps of each machine and is an observation, not a proof (holdouts/related.py, holdouts/related.json).

Same table as the machines below, started in another state. Renaming the states as shown turns this machine's table into the other one, the halting transition included. The other machine starts in its own state A, which is not this machine's A: its run from blank tape is the run of this table started in another state. These are different runs: in the first 107 steps of each, no configuration of this machine's run occurs in any of the others, even up to a shift of the tape. So each of these holdouts is its own halting question, and settling one does not settle another.

  • 1RB0RA_1LC0RE_0LD0LB_1LA1LF_1RA0LF_1LC---: rename A→E, B→A, C→B, D→C, E→D, F→F; it is this table started in state B
  • 1RB1RF_1LC0LB_1RE0LD_1LB0RF_0RA0RC_1RE---: rename A→D, B→B, C→C, D→E, E→A, F→F and exchange left and right; it is this table started in state E, in a mirror
  • 1RB0LE_0RC0RA_1RD1RF_1LA0LD_1LD0RF_1RB---: rename A→E, B→D, C→A, D→B, E→C, F→F and exchange left and right; it is this table started in state C, in a mirror

summary: Bouncer over a list of counters written as runs of 01 or 10: the first run grows by one every three left-end visits, the second at half that rate, the third shrinks while the fourth grows, and short irregular words sit at the right end. No regime proved yet.
family: bouncer over a list of 01/10 counters
